headline: Both render engines can be driven from code and Gate 1 was signed on 2026-10-14: Helix Native 3.82 renders a captured chain (about 1.9 s per 2 s clip, fixed reset cost plus 0.045 s per second of audio) and the HX Stomp (firmware 3.50, macOS only) renders over USB (about 2.7 s per clip); a generated .hlx was accepted by HX Edit and loaded on the pedal. Around that sit unit-tested but unproven building blocks: a preset parser and validator, a guitar separator, a section segmenter, a reference-DI picker, a loss kit and a CMA-ES search that now plans serially against the real render cost. Since the first report the envelope loss term was rebuilt (v1) but on non-Helix proxy signals its held-out rank-1 is only 0.033 to 0.117 on fresh seeds, so it is still weak and no loss term is admitted (every default weight is 0). Nothing has been measured on real songs or on a Helix-rendered known-answer set; there is no song-to-preset command; Gates 2 and 3 have no evidence; nothing has been judged by ear. The human's next actions are to capture three Native chains, approve the synthetic-benchmark thresholds, download a DI set, give the go on the T018 spike and the AFx-Rep checkpoint, read the installer EULAs, decide the firmware and the project licence.

features.name: Helix Native engine
features.purpose: Render a DI clip through a candidate preset offline in Helix Native, fast enough to be the searching engine.
features.done_when: A NativeEngine behind the frozen interface renders any chain structure the search needs at a measured cost, loads candidates without a GUI step per candidate, agrees with the Stomp within a measured null residual, and has run a full synthetic recovery pass.
features.completion_reason: Hosting, replay and 16+16 automation work, engine-smoke is green, and the cost() cache bug that made search's demo look 5x slower is fixed and re-measured. Still: each new chain structure needs one manual GUI capture, only an empty preset and known.hlx were measured, whole-preset write is rejected, T018 (easier load route) is unstarted awaiting the human's go, and no recovery run or parity null exists.
features.functionality: Renders a 2 s DI through a GUI-captured chain template with automated knob and switch values (about 1.87 s per render: fixed ~1.80 s reset plus ~0.045 s per second of audio; set_params 0.5 ms; pool about 2.0 to 2.1 renders/s at 6 processes; replay null -72.9 dB in a fresh process); cost() is cached per chain structure. Cannot load an arbitrary preset or a new chain structure without a human GUI step.

challenges.finding: Whole-preset state write is impossible: the saved state is opaque high-entropy records in a CMXH container, and replayed library records are refused. Going further would mean attacking the cipher, which the interop-only rule forbids.

Every render is a reset render with a 4,800-sample pre-roll; reset costs about 1.6 s regardless of clip length, so cost() not clip length sets the budget. Measured on an empty preset and one chain: a lower bound.

cost() was cached by raw-state hash; a knob move changes Native's raw state, so plan_budget re-ran a ~130-156 s measurement inside search's smoke demo (156 of 202 s). Fixed by keying on chain structure; demo went to 46 s, 2.4 s per render call, same answer. Loaded-machine runs (two foreign CPU-bound jobs) are 1.96 s, so timings vary about 5 percent with load.
Throughput scales to about 2.3 renders/s at 6 to 8 workers; parallel use inside CI is not measured.
Native EULA is silent on training ML on Native renders; installer EULAs unread.
